proxy_language: Proto-Chibchan / Barbacoan-Paezan reconstruction (Chibchan-centered, Lower Central American/Colombian Pacific branch), with Quechua-substrate caution
proxy_rationale: Las Vegas culture (c. 10,000-6,600 BP, Santa Elena Peninsula) is known only archaeologically; its language is unattested and unrecoverable. The most defensible weak proxies are the Chibchan family (Constenla Umana 1981, Pache and colleagues) and neighbouring Barbacoan languages (Cayapa/Chachi, Tsafiki/Colorado), the only non-Quechuan, non-Cariban families plausibly rooted in the Ecuadorian coast and northern Andes. The link is extremely tenuous: 8,000+ years of time depth, with later Quechua, Cara and Manteno overlays.
phonology: Modelled on Proto-Chibchan (Constenla Umana 1981; Pache 2018) with Barbacoan flavour. Consonants: p t k, b d g (limited), ts tsh/ch, s, h, m n, l r, w y; an implosive/glottal element is often reconstructed. Vowels: i e a o u, with a central vowel written ɨ/u-bar in Chibchan; nasal and long vowels appear in daughters. Tone absent in the reconstruction (Barbacoan Tsafiki has a pitch accent). Treat all values as heuristic.
phonotactics: Mostly open syllables CV, CVC, V. Word-initial single consonants only, no initial clusters. Medial clusters limited to nasal+stop (mb nd ng), s/h+stop, or liquid+stop across a syllable boundary. Final consonants limited to n, s, k, l, r, and vowels are most frequent. No long consonant clusters; roots typically 1-2 syllables, derived words 2-3.
orthography: Practical Latin transliteration of the Chibchan/Barbacoan tradition: p t k b d g ch ts s h m n l r w y; vowels a e i o u, with ɨ written as 'ü' or 'ii'. Glottal stop as an apostrophe. No q, x, f, v, z, j. This is a reconstruction-style spelling, not an attested orthography.
morphology: Proto-Chibchan is agglutinating with SOV order, mostly suffixing, postpositions, and a small set of nominal suffixes: plural/collective (-ka/-ko type), locative (-ba/-ka, 'place'), genitive by juxtaposition with possessor first. Roots are monosyllabic or disyllabic; reduplication is attested in Chibchan for plurality and intensity. No grammatical gender; some animacy marking.
compounding: Compounding is by juxtaposition, with the modifier or possessor first and the head last (Chibchan and Barbacoan pattern). 'X of Y' is Y + X; 'Y-maker' is Y + agentive/verb root with a nominalizer such as -wa or -ka; place names take a locative suffix -ba/-ka; no linker is required, though a vowel may be inserted to split clusters (e.g., -a- or -i-).
noun_phrase_order: Modifier-head: possessor/genitive before head noun, adjective or attributive before noun, numeral before noun; function morphemes follow the noun as suffixes.

attested_roots.gloss: locative / place, also mother in some branches

sources: Constenla Umana, Adolfo. 1981. Comparative Chibchan Phonology (PhD diss., University of Pennsylvania)
Pache, Matthias. 2018. Contributions to Chibchan Historical Linguistics (Leiden/LOT)
Curnow, Timothy and Liddicoat, Anthony. 1998. The Barbacoan Languages of Colombia and Ecuador. Anthropological Linguistics
Dickinson, Connie. 2002. Complex Predicates in Tsafiki (PhD diss., University of Oregon)
Stothert, Karen. 1985. The Preceramic Las Vegas Culture of Coastal Ecuador. American Antiquity
notes: The Las Vegas culture language is entirely unknown; names are speculative and flavoured by Chibchan/Barbacoan phonotactics only. Most roots are reconstructed or approximate and should be marked as such. Quechua, Spanish and other modern words should be avoided. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word, since the language is not Goidelic.
